36/// nothing else. Past it, as any cycle goes, the object reads as a missing one.

52/// Parse the "root" xref from the PDF.
53///
54/// PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (45)) also whether the table was rebuilt because the newest
55/// section cuts off the page tree (see below).
56pub(crate) fn root_xref(data: PdfData, password: &[u8]) -> Result<(XRef, bool), XRefError> {
57    let mut xref_map = FxHashMap::default();
58    let xref_pos = find_last_xref_pos(data.as_ref()).ok_or(XRefError::Unknown)?;
59    let trailer = populate_xref_impl(data.as_ref(), xref_pos, &mut xref_map).ok_or(XRefError::Unknown)?;
60    // PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (45)) whether the newest section names an earlier one. Its
61    // `/XRefStm` (a hybrid file's stream, §7.5.8.4) belongs to the same update and doesn't count,
62    // as `pdfcraft-cos` doesn't count it.
63    let linked = Reader::new(trailer)
64        .read_with_context::<Dict<'_>>(&ReaderContext::dummy())
65        .is_some_and(|newest| prev_offset(data.as_ref(), &newest, &XrefMap::default()).is_some());
66
67    let xref = XRef::new(data.clone(), xref_map, XRefInput::TrailerDictData(trailer), false, password)?;
68    // PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (45)) an update whose section has no `/Prev` (ISO 32000-2
69    // §7.5.6, §7.5.8.2) cuts off the revisions before it, and with them the page tree its catalog
70    // names (the signed files of PDFBOX-2720 and PDFBOX-2942). The table is rebuilt by scanning
71    // the file, as for a broken one, so the page tree is found rather than whatever page
72    // dictionaries `Pages::new_brute_force` turns up. Only when that section names no earlier
73    // one, the file holds another `startxref`, and the page tree can't be read: the conditions
74    // `pdfcraft-cos` rebuilds under, so the two agree on the pages.
75    let cut_off = !linked && xref.get::<Dict<'_>>(xref.trailer_data().pages_ref).is_none() && more_than_one_startxref(data.as_ref());
76    if cut_off {
77        warn!("the newest xref section has no Prev and the page tree is unreachable; rebuilding the xref table");
78        xref.repair();
79    }
80    Ok((xref, cut_off))
81}
82
83/// PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (45)) whether `data` holds an earlier `startxref` than its last.
84fn more_than_one_startxref(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
85    let needle = b"startxref";
86    findr_needle(data, needle)
87        .and_then(|last| data.get(..last))
88        .is_some_and(|before| crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::util::find_needle(before, needle).is_some())
89}

91/// Try to manually parse the PDF to build an xref table and trailer dictionary.
92pub(crate) fn fallback(data: PdfData, password: &[u8]) -> Option<XRef> {
93    warn!("xref table was invalid, trying to manually build xref table");
94    let (xref_map, xref_input) = fallback_xref_map(&data, password);
95
96    if let Some(xref_input) = xref_input {
97        warn!("rebuild xref table with {} entries", xref_map.len());
98
99        XRef::new(data.clone(), xref_map, xref_input, true, password).ok()
100    } else {
101        warn!("couldn't find trailer dictionary, failed to rebuild xref table");
102
103        None
104    }
105}

107/// PdfCraft patch: an `N G obj` header for the repair scan, taking a generation number that
108/// cannot be read as 0.
109///
110/// A generation number is at most 65,535 (ISO 32000-2 §7.5.4), so `3 18446744073709551616 obj` is
111/// malformed and [`ObjectIdentifier::read`] is right to refuse it everywhere else. This scan runs
112/// only when a file's cross-reference table is unusable and its objects are being recovered by
113/// reading the file, where refusing the header drops the object and whatever it holds (#5580).
114/// Before #427 the digits wrapped, and 2^64 wrapped to exactly 0, which is the only reason such a
115/// file used to open.
116///
117/// Only here: reading numbers anywhere else is unchanged.
118fn read_object_header<'a>(r: &mut Reader<'a>, ctx: &ReaderContext<'a>) -> Option<ObjectIdentifier> {
119    let mut strict = r.clone();
120    if let Some(obj_id) = strict.read::<ObjectIdentifier>(ctx) {
121        *r = strict;
122        return Some(obj_id);
123    }
124    // On a clone as well, so a header that isn't one leaves `r` where it was for the caller.
125    let mut lenient = r.clone();
126    let obj_number = lenient.read_without_context::<i32>()?;
127    lenient.skip_white_spaces_and_comments();
128    // Any number at all in the generation position, including one no generation may be.
129    lenient.skip::<Number>(false)?;
130    lenient.skip_white_spaces_and_comments();
131    lenient.forward_tag(b"obj")?;
132    *r = lenient;
133    Some(ObjectIdentifier::new(obj_number, 0))
134}

136/// PdfCraft patch: the body of the object at `offset` whose `N G obj` header cannot be read
137/// strictly, for a table rebuilt by scanning the file (#5580). The steps are
138/// `IndirectObject::read`'s, with [`read_object_header`] in place of the strict identifier.
139fn read_repaired_body<'a, T>(data: &'a [u8], offset: usize, id: ObjectIdentifier, ctx: &ReaderContext<'a>) -> Option<T>
140where
141    T: ObjectLike<'a>,
142{
143    let mut r = Reader::new(data);
144    r.jump(offset);
145    // The number is what identifies the object; the generation is what could not be read.
146    if read_object_header(&mut r, ctx)?.obj_number != id.obj_number {
147        return None;
148    }
149    let mut ctx = ctx.clone();
150    if ctx.parent_chain_contains(&id) {
151        warn!("cycle detected in indirect object: {id:?}");
152
153        return None;
154    }
155    ctx.set_obj_number(id);
156    ctx.parent_chain_push(id);
157    r.skip_white_spaces_and_comments();
158    r.read_with_context::<T>(&ctx)
159}

161fn fallback_xref_map<'a>(data: &'a PdfData, password: &[u8]) -> (XrefMap, Option<XRefInput<'a>>) {
162    fallback_xref_map_inner(data, ReaderContext::dummy(), true, password)
163}
164
165fn fallback_xref_map_inner<'a>(
166    data: &'a PdfData,
167    mut dummy_ctx: ReaderContext<'a>,
168    recurse: bool,
169    password: &[u8],
170) -> (XrefMap, Option<XRefInput<'a>>) {
171    let mut xref_map = FxHashMap::default();
172    // PdfCraft patch: the generation-0 keys below that stand in for a header with another
173    // generation, so a later header can replace one while a real `N 0 obj` is never displaced
174    // (noted in review of #5580).
175    let mut aliases: rustc_hash::FxHashSet<ObjectIdentifier> = rustc_hash::FxHashSet::default();
176    let mut trailer_dicts = vec![];
177    let mut root_ref = None;
178
179    let mut r = Reader::new(data.as_ref());
180
181    let mut last_obj_num = None;
182
183    loop {
184        let cur_pos = r.offset();
185
186        let mut old_r = r.clone();
187
188        // First try to check if we have an object identifier.
189        if r.peek_byte().is_some_and(|b: u8| b.is_ascii_digit()) {
190            if let Some(obj_id) = read_object_header(&mut r, &dummy_ctx) {
191                let mut cloned = r.clone();
192                // Check that the object following it is actually valid before inserting it.
193                cloned.skip_white_spaces_and_comments();
194                if cloned.skip::<Object<'_>>(false).is_some() {
195                    xref_map.insert(obj_id, EntryType::Normal(cur_pos));
196                    // PdfCraft patch: also reachable by object number alone, so a reference that
197                    // names a different generation than the header still finds it. A rebuilt
198                    // table has no revision history to tell two generations apart, and a file
199                    // that needs rebuilding references everything as `N 0 R` whatever its headers
200                    // say: `poppler-85140-0.pdf` has one page whose header reads
201                    // `3 18446744073709551616 obj` with a page tree pointing at `3 0 R`, so the
202                    // page was lost and the file did not open at all (#5580). `or_insert`, so a
203                    // real `N 0 obj` is never displaced by this alias.
204                    let by_number = ObjectIdentifier::new(obj_id.obj_number, 0);
205                    if obj_id.gen_number == 0 {
206                        // A real `N 0 obj`: it owns the key from here on, and the last one wins
207                        // as every other entry does.
208                        aliases.remove(&by_number);
209                    } else if !xref_map.contains_key(&by_number) || aliases.contains(&by_number) {
210                        // Stand in for it, and let a later header for the same number replace the
211                        // stand-in -- the exact key moves on, so an alias left behind would send
212                        // `N 0 R` to a body the exact key no longer names (noted in review).
213                        xref_map.insert(by_number, EntryType::Normal(cur_pos));
214                        aliases.insert(by_number);
215                    }
216                    last_obj_num = Some(obj_id);
217                    dummy_ctx.set_obj_number(obj_id);
218                }
219            } else {
220                // There must be a white space before the next object number.
221                r.forward_while(|b| !is_white_space_character(b));
222            }
223        } else {
224            // Then, try to check whether we have a dictionary, in particular a trailer
225            // dictionary.
226            let mut probe_reader = r.clone();
227            if r.peek_bytes(2).is_some_and(|b| b == b"<<")
228                && let Some(probe) = { probe_dict(&mut probe_reader, &dummy_ctx, Some(b"<<"), b">>") }
229            {
230                r = probe_reader;
231                if probe.has_root || probe.has_type {
232                    let mut dict_reader = Reader::new(probe.data);
233                    if let Some(dict) = dict_reader.read_with_context::<Dict<'_>>(&dummy_ctx) {
234                        if probe.has_root && dict.contains_key(ROOT) {
235                            trailer_dicts.push(dict.clone());
236                        }
237
238                        if dict.get::<Name<'_>>(TYPE).is_some_and(|n| n.as_str() == "Catalog") {
239                            root_ref = last_obj_num;
240                        }
241
242                        if let Some(stream) = old_r.read::<Stream<'_>>(&dummy_ctx)
243                            && dict.get::<Name<'_>>(TYPE).as_deref() == Some(b"ObjStm")
244                            && let Some(data) = stream.decoded().ok()
245                            && let Some(last_obj_num) = last_obj_num
246                            && let Some(obj_stream) = ObjectStream::new(stream, &data, &dummy_ctx)
247                        {
248                            for (idx, (obj_num, _)) in obj_stream.offsets.iter().enumerate() {
249                                let id = ObjectIdentifier::new(*obj_num as i32, 0);
250                                // If we already found an entry for that object number that was not
251                                // inside an object stream. Somewhat arbitrary and maybe
252                                // we can do better, but that seems to work for the current
253                                // set of tests.
254                                if xref_map.get(&id).is_none_or(|e| !matches!(e, &EntryType::Normal(_))) {
255                                    xref_map.insert(id, EntryType::ObjStream(last_obj_num.obj_number as u32, idx as u32));
256                                }
257                            }
258                        }
259                    }
260                }
261            } else {
262                // We can skip everything until the next white space character,
263                // as there cannot possibly be any new dictionary/object identifier
264                // until then.
265                let old_pos = r.offset;
266                r.forward_while(|b| !is_white_space_character(b));
267                if r.offset == old_pos {
268                    r.read_byte();
269                }
270            }
271        }
272
273        if r.at_end() {
274            break;
275        }
276    }
277
278    // Try to choose the right trailer dict by doing basic validation.
279    let mut trailer_dict = None;
280
281    for dict in trailer_dicts {
282        if let Some(root_id) = dict.get_raw::<Dict<'_>>(ROOT) {
283            let check = |dict: &Dict<'_>| -> bool { dict.contains_key(PAGES) };
284
285            match root_id {
286                MaybeRef::Ref(r) => match xref_map.get(&r.into()) {
287                    Some(EntryType::Normal(offset)) => {
288                        let mut reader = Reader::new(&data.as_ref()[*offset..]);
289
290                        if let Some(obj) = reader.read_with_context::<IndirectObject<Dict<'_>>>(&dummy_ctx)
291                            && {
292                                let obj = obj.get();
293                                check(&obj)
294                            }
295                        {
296                            trailer_dict = Some(dict);
297                        }
298                    }
299                    Some(EntryType::ObjStream(obj_num, idx)) => {
300                        if let Some(EntryType::Normal(offset)) = xref_map.get(&ObjectIdentifier::new(*obj_num as i32, 0)) {
301                            let mut reader = Reader::new(&data.as_ref()[*offset..]);
302
303                            if let Some(stream) = reader.read_with_context::<IndirectObject<Stream<'_>>>(&dummy_ctx)
304                                && {
305                                    let stream = stream.get();
306                                    if let Some(data) = stream.decoded().ok()
307                                        && let Some(object_stream) = ObjectStream::new(stream, &data, &dummy_ctx)
308                                        && let Some(obj) = object_stream.get::<Dict<'_>>(*idx)
309                                    {
310                                        check(&obj)
311                                    } else {
312                                        false
313                                    }
314                                }
315                            {
316                                trailer_dict = Some(dict);
317                            }
318                        }
319                    }
320                    _ => {}
321                },
322                MaybeRef::NotRef(d) => {
323                    if check(&d) {
324                        trailer_dict = Some(dict);
325                    }
326                }
327            }
328        }
329    }
330
331    let has_encryption = trailer_dict.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.contains_key(ENCRYPT));
332
333    if has_encryption && recurse {
334        // The problem is that in this case, we have used a dummy reader context which does not have
335        // a decryptor. Therefore, we were unable to decrypt any of the object streams and missed
336        // all objects that are inside of such a stream. Therefore, we need to redo the process
337        // using a `ReaderContext` that does have the ability to decrypt.
338        if let Ok(xref) =
339            XRef::new(data.clone(), xref_map.clone(), XRefInput::TrailerDictData(trailer_dict.as_ref().map(|d| d.data()).unwrap()), true, password)
340        {
341            let ctx = ReaderContext::new(&xref, false);
342            let (patched_map, _) = fallback_xref_map_inner(data, ctx, false, password);
343            xref_map = patched_map;
344        }
345    }
346
347    if let Some(trailer_dict_data) = trailer_dict.map(|d| d.data()) {
348        (xref_map, Some(XRefInput::TrailerDictData(trailer_dict_data)))
349    } else if let Some(root_ref) = root_ref {
350        (xref_map, Some(XRefInput::RootRef(root_ref)))
351    } else {
352        (xref_map, None)
353    }
354}

356const DUMMY_XREF: XRef = XRef(Inner::Dummy);
357
358/// An xref table.
359#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
360pub struct XRef(Inner);
361
362impl XRef {
363    // PdfCraft patch: keep the bounded dictionary-index cache local to this PDF.
364    pub(crate) fn with_dict_cache<T>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut DictCache) -> T) -> Option<T> {
365        let Inner::Some(repr) = &self.0 else {
366            return None;
367        };
368        let mut cache = repr.dict_cache.lock().unwrap_or_else(|poison| poison.into_inner());
369        #[cfg(any())]
370        let mut cache = repr.dict_cache.try_borrow_mut().ok()?;
371        Some(f(&mut cache))
372    }
373
374    /// PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (22)) run `f` on this PDF's parsed object stream indexes
375    /// ([`ObjectStreamIndexes`]). `None` when there is none to use (the dummy xref, or a no_std
376    /// cache already borrowed), and the caller then parses the index without it. A poisoned lock
377    /// is still used: entries are complete `Arc`s inserted in one step, so a panic elsewhere
378    /// cannot have left one half-written.
379    fn with_object_stream_indexes<T>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut ObjectStreamIndexes) -> T) -> Option<T> {
380        let Inner::Some(repr) = &self.0 else {
381            return None;
382        };
383        let mut indexes = repr.object_stream_indexes.lock().unwrap_or_else(|poison| poison.into_inner());
384        #[cfg(any())]
385        let mut indexes = repr.object_stream_indexes.try_borrow_mut().ok()?;
386        Some(f(&mut indexes))
387    }
388
389    fn new(data: PdfData, xref_map: XrefMap, input: XRefInput<'_>, repaired: bool, password: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, XRefError> {
390        // This is a bit hacky, but the problem is we can't read the resolved trailer dictionary
391        // before we actually created the xref struct. So we first create it using dummy data
392        // and then populate the data.
393        let trailer_data = TrailerData::dummy();
394
395        let mut xref = Self(Inner::Some(Arc::new(SomeRepr {
396            data: Arc::new(Data::new(data)),
397            map: Arc::new(RwLock::new(MapRepr { xref_map, repaired })),
398            decryptor: Arc::new(Decryptor::None),
399            has_ocgs: false,
400            metadata: Arc::new(Metadata::default()),
401            trailer_data,
402            password: password.to_vec(),
403            dict_cache: Arc::new(Mutex::new(DictCache::default())),
404            object_stream_indexes: Arc::new(Mutex::new(ObjectStreamIndexes::default())),
405        })));
406
407        // We read the trailer twice, once to determine the encryption used and then a second
408        // time to resolve the catalog dictionary, etc. This allows us to support catalog dictionaries
409        // that are stored in an encrypted object stream.
410
411        let decryptor = {
412            match input {
413                XRefInput::TrailerDictData(trailer_dict_data) => {
414                    let mut r = Reader::new(trailer_dict_data);
415
416                    let trailer_dict = r.read_with_context::<Dict<'_>>(&ReaderContext::new(&xref, false)).ok_or(XRefError::Unknown)?;
417
418                    get_decryptor(&trailer_dict, password)?
419                }
420                XRefInput::RootRef(_) => Decryptor::None,
421            }
422        };
423
424        match &mut xref.0 {
425            Inner::Dummy => unreachable!(),
426            Inner::Some(r) => {
427                let mutable = Arc::make_mut(r);
428                mutable.decryptor = Arc::new(decryptor.clone());
429            }
430        }
431
432        let (trailer_data, has_ocgs, metadata) = match input {
433            XRefInput::TrailerDictData(trailer_dict_data) => {
434                let mut r = Reader::new(trailer_dict_data);
435
436                let trailer_dict = r.read_with_context::<Dict<'_>>(&ReaderContext::new(&xref, false)).ok_or(XRefError::Unknown)?;
437
438                let root_ref = trailer_dict.get_ref(ROOT).ok_or(XRefError::Unknown)?;
439                let root = trailer_dict.get::<Dict<'_>>(ROOT).ok_or(XRefError::Unknown)?;
440                let metadata = trailer_dict.get::<Dict<'_>>(INFO).map(|d| parse_metadata(&d)).unwrap_or_default();
441                let pages_ref = root.get_ref(PAGES).ok_or(XRefError::Unknown)?;
442                let has_ocgs = root.get::<Dict<'_>>(OCPROPERTIES).is_some();
443                let version = root.get::<Name<'_>>(VERSION).and_then(|v| PdfVersion::from_bytes(v.deref()));
444
445                let td = TrailerData { pages_ref: pages_ref.into(), root_ref: root_ref.into(), version };
446
447                (td, has_ocgs, metadata)
448            }
449            XRefInput::RootRef(root_ref) => {
450                let root = xref.get::<Dict<'_>>(root_ref).ok_or(XRefError::Unknown)?;
451                let pages_ref = root.get_ref(PAGES).ok_or(XRefError::Unknown)?;
452
453                let td = TrailerData { pages_ref: pages_ref.into(), root_ref, version: None };
454
455                (td, false, Metadata::default())
456            }
457        };
458
459        match &mut xref.0 {
460            Inner::Dummy => unreachable!(),
461            Inner::Some(r) => {
462                let mutable = Arc::make_mut(r);
463                mutable.trailer_data = trailer_data;
464                mutable.decryptor = Arc::new(decryptor);
465                mutable.has_ocgs = has_ocgs;
466                mutable.metadata = Arc::new(metadata);
467            }
468        }
469
470        Ok(xref)
471    }

473    pub(crate) fn dummy() -> &'static Self {
474        &DUMMY_XREF
475    }

477    pub(crate) fn len(&self) -> usize {
478        match &self.0 {
479            Inner::Dummy => 0,
480            Inner::Some(r) => r.map.get().xref_map.len(),
481        }
482    }
483
484    pub(crate) fn trailer_data(&self) -> &TrailerData {
485        match &self.0 {
486            Inner::Dummy => unreachable!(),
487            Inner::Some(r) => &r.trailer_data,
488        }
489    }
490
491    pub(crate) fn metadata(&self) -> &Metadata {
492        match &self.0 {
493            Inner::Dummy => unreachable!(),
494            Inner::Some(r) => &r.metadata,
495        }
496    }
497
498    /// Return the object ID of the root dictionary.
499    pub fn root_id(&self) -> ObjectIdentifier {
500        self.trailer_data().root_ref
501    }
502
503    /// Whether the PDF has optional content groups.
504    pub fn has_optional_content_groups(&self) -> bool {
505        match &self.0 {
506            Inner::Dummy => false,
507            Inner::Some(r) => r.has_ocgs,
508        }
509    }
510
511    pub(crate) fn objects(&self) -> impl IntoIterator<Item = Object<'_>> + '_ {
512        match &self.0 {
513            Inner::Dummy => unimplemented!(),
514            Inner::Some(r) => {
515                let locked = r.map.get();
516                let mut elements = locked
517                    .xref_map
518                    .iter()
519                    .map(|(id, e)| {
520                        let offset = match e {
521                            EntryType::Normal(o) => (*o, 0),
522                            EntryType::ObjStream(id, index) => {
523                                if let Some(EntryType::Normal(offset)) = locked.xref_map.get(&ObjectIdentifier::new(*id as i32, 0)) {
524                                    (*offset, *index)
525                                } else {
526                                    (usize::MAX, 0)
527                                }
528                            }
529                        };
530
531                        (*id, offset)
532                    })
533                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
534
535                // Try to yield in the order the objects appeared in the
536                // PDF.
537                elements.sort_by(|e1, e2| e1.1.cmp(&e2.1));
538                // PdfCraft patch: one object per location. A rebuilt table can hold two keys for
539                // one object -- its own generation and the generation-0 stand-in (#5580) -- and
540                // enumeration yielded the object once for each, so a document recovered by
541                // `Pages::new_brute_force` reported the page twice (noted in review). Both keys
542                // stay for lookups; only this walk is deduplicated. The object number is part of
543                // the key: an object stream at (offset, 0) and its first member, also
544                // (offset, 0), are two objects.
545                elements.dedup_by(|a, b| a.1 == b.1 && a.0.obj_number == b.0.obj_number);
546
547                let mut iter = elements.into_iter();
548
549                iter::from_fn(move || {
550                    for next in iter.by_ref() {
551                        // PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (33)) an object that only refers to another
552                        // isn't one of its own: followed, that one came out once more for each.
553                        if let Some(Fetched::Object(obj)) = self.fetch(next.0, &ReaderContext::new(self, false)) {
554                            return Some(obj);
555                        } else {
556                            // Skip invalid objects.
557                            continue;
558                        }
559                    }
560
561                    None
562                })
563            }
564        }
565    }
566
567    pub(crate) fn repair(&self) {
568        let Inner::Some(r) = &self.0 else {
569            return;
570        };
571
572        // All callers release read guards before following references/repairing.
573        // Fallback reconstruction uses its own dummy/temporary xref, never this
574        // locked map. Serialize the one repair and let concurrent readers wait.
575        let mut locked = r.map.put();
576        if locked.repaired {
577            return;
578        }
579        // Set first so an unwinding fallback cannot trigger a reparse storm.
580        // Assignment below publishes a complete replacement atomically.
581        locked.repaired = true;
582        let (xref_map, _) = fallback_xref_map(r.data.get(), &r.password);
583        locked.xref_map = xref_map;
584    }
585
586    /// PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (43)) whether objects read through this table are
587    /// decrypted.
588    pub(crate) fn is_encrypted(&self) -> bool {
589        match &self.0 {
590            Inner::Dummy => false,
591            Inner::Some(r) => !matches!(r.decryptor.as_ref(), Decryptor::None),
592        }
593    }
594
595    #[inline]
596    pub(crate) fn needs_decryption(&self, ctx: &ReaderContext<'_>) -> bool {
597        match &self.0 {
598            Inner::Dummy => false,
599            Inner::Some(r) => {
600                if matches!(r.decryptor.as_ref(), Decryptor::None) {
601                    false
602                } else {
603                    !ctx.in_content_stream() && !ctx.in_object_stream()
604                }
605            }
606        }
607    }
608
609    #[inline]
610    pub(crate) fn decrypt(&self, id: ObjectIdentifier, data: &[u8], target: DecryptionTarget<'_>) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
611        match &self.0 {
612            Inner::Dummy => Some(data.to_vec()),
613            Inner::Some(r) => r.decryptor.decrypt(id, data, target),
614        }
615    }
616
617    /// Return the object with the given identifier.
618    #[allow(private_bounds)]
619    pub fn get<'a, T>(&'a self, id: ObjectIdentifier) -> Option<T>
620    where
621        T: ObjectLike<'a>,
622    {
623        let ctx = ReaderContext::new(self, false);
624        self.get_with(id, &ctx)
625    }
626
627    /// Return the object with the given identifier.
628    ///
629    /// PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (33)) an object that holds only a reference stands for what
630    /// that names. Read as a number it was the reference's own object number, and as anything else
631    /// it was lost. This is a loop, so a long chain takes no stack.
632    #[allow(private_bounds)]
633    pub(crate) fn get_with<'a, T>(&'a self, id: ObjectIdentifier, ctx: &ReaderContext<'a>) -> Option<T>
634    where
635        T: ObjectLike<'a>,
636    {
637        let mut id = id;
638        for _ in 0..=MAX_REFERENCE_HOPS {
639            match self.fetch::<T>(id, ctx)? {
640                Fetched::Object(object) => return Some(object),
641                Fetched::Reference(next) => id = next,
642            }
643        }
644        warn!("references lead on past the limit, or in a cycle: {id:?}");
645
646        None
647    }
648
649    /// PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (33)) the object stream `id`. It has to be a stream stored as
650    /// that object (ISO 32000-2 7.5.7), so this follows no reference: the check of where it is stored
651    /// is of that object, and one reached through a reference could be a stream stored inside
652    /// another.
653    pub(crate) fn object_stream<'a>(&'a self, id: ObjectIdentifier, ctx: &ReaderContext<'a>) -> Option<Stream<'a>> {
654        match self.fetch::<Stream<'a>>(id, ctx)? {
655            Fetched::Object(stream) => Some(stream),
656            Fetched::Reference(_) => None,
657        }
658    }
659
660    /// What is stored at the object with the given identifier.
661    fn fetch<'a, T>(&'a self, id: ObjectIdentifier, ctx: &ReaderContext<'a>) -> Option<Fetched<T>>
662    where
663        T: ObjectLike<'a>,
664    {
665        let Inner::Some(repr) = &self.0 else {
666            return None;
667        };
668
669        let locked = repr.map.get();
670
671        let mut r = Reader::new(repr.data.get().as_ref());
672
673        let entry = *locked.xref_map.get(&id).or({
674            // An indirect reference to an undefined object shall not be considered an error by a PDF processor; it
675            // shall be treated as a reference to the null object.
676            None
677        })?;
678        let repaired = locked.repaired;
679        drop(locked);
680
681        let mut ctx = ctx.clone();
682        ctx.set_obj_number(id);
683        ctx.set_in_content_stream(false);
684
685        match entry {
686            EntryType::Normal(offset) => {
687                ctx.set_in_object_stream(false);
688                r.jump(offset);
689
690                if let Some(next) = held_reference(r.clone(), id) {
691                    return Some(Fetched::Reference(next));
692                }
693
694                if let Some(object) = r.read_with_context::<IndirectObject<T>>(&ctx) {
695                    // PdfCraft patch: in a table rebuilt by scanning the file, the object number
696                    // is what identifies an object. There is no revision history to tell two
697                    // generations apart, the scan already files objects found in object streams
698                    // under generation 0, and a malformed generation in a header would otherwise
699                    // make the object unreadable through the reference that names it (#5580). A
700                    // table read from the file's own xref keeps the exact match.
701                    if object.id() == &id || (repaired && object.id().obj_number == id.obj_number) {
702                        return Some(Fetched::Object(object.get()));
703                    }
704                } else {
705                    // PdfCraft patch: the strict read of the header failed. In a table rebuilt by
706                    // scanning the file that can be a generation number no generation may be --
707                    // `3 18446744073709551616 obj` -- and refusing it loses the object the
708                    // reference names (#5580). The object number still has to be the one asked
709                    // for; only an unreadable generation is tolerated, and only here.
710                    if repaired && let Some(object) = read_repaired_body::<T>(repr.data.get().as_ref(), offset, id, &ctx) {
711                        return Some(Fetched::Object(object));
712                    }
713                    // There is a valid object at the offset, it's just not of the type the caller
714                    // expected, which is fine.
715                    if r.skip::<IndirectObject<Object<'_>>>(false).is_some() {
716                        return None;
717                    }
718                };
719
720                // The xref table is broken, try to repair if not already repaired.
721                if repaired {
722                    error!("attempt was made at repairing xref, but object {id:?} still couldn't be read");
723
724                    None
725                } else {
726                    warn!("broken xref, attempting to repair");
727
728                    self.repair();
729
730                    // Now try reading again.
731                    self.fetch::<T>(id, &ctx)
732                }
733            }
734            EntryType::ObjStream(obj_stram_gen_num, index) => {
735                // Generation number is implicitly 0.
736                let obj_stream_id = ObjectIdentifier::new(obj_stram_gen_num as i32, 0);
737
738                if obj_stream_id == id {
739                    warn!("cycle detected in object stream");
740
741                    return None;
742                }
743
744                // Stream objects cannot themselves be stored in object streams
745                // (PDF 7.5.7). Reject malformed chains before recursively loading
746                // them, including A-in-B/B-in-A and arbitrarily deep chains.
747                if !matches!(repr.map.get().xref_map.get(&obj_stream_id), Some(EntryType::Normal(_))) {
748                    return None;
749                }
750
751                // PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (22)) the stream's index of `objnum offset` pairs
752                // is parsed once and kept, as its decoded data is: parsed again for every object
753                // fetched from it, reading all of a stream of N objects took N² steps (one
754                // Firefox page kept 65,542 objects in one stream and took 37 s to draw).
755                let data = repr.data.get_with(obj_stream_id, &ctx)?;
756                let known = self.with_object_stream_indexes(|indexes| indexes.get(&obj_stream_id).cloned()).flatten();
757                let offsets = match known {
758                    // A stream whose pairs don't parse stays unreadable, as it was.
759                    Some(offsets) => offsets?,
760                    None => {
761                        // PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (33)) this read can reach another object
762                        // stream, whose `/N` or `/First` can be a member of the next: the gate's
763                        // limit holds here too, or a chain of them ran out of stack. It reads the
764                        // dictionary, which is all it needs: parsing the stream reads `/Length`
765                        // too, a second way to the next stream's index, which doubled at each.
766                        let _loading = repr.data.enter_loading(obj_stream_id)?;
767                        let Fetched::Object(dict) = self.fetch::<Dict<'_>>(obj_stream_id, &ctx)? else {
768                            return None;
769                        };
770                        // `/N` and `/First` may be references that can't be followed while
771                        // another stream loads: reading them fails without being remembered.
772                        let num_objects = dict.get::<usize>(N)?;
773                        let first_offset = dict.get::<usize>(FIRST)?;
774                        let parsed = read_object_stream_index(num_objects, first_offset, data).map(Arc::new);
775                        self.with_object_stream_indexes(|indexes| indexes.entry(obj_stream_id).or_insert_with(|| parsed.clone()).clone())
776                            .unwrap_or(parsed)?
777                    }
778                };
779                let stream = ObjectStream::with_offsets(data, &ctx, offsets);
780                if let Some(next) = stream.reference(index) {
781                    return Some(Fetched::Reference(next));
782                }
783
784                stream.get(index).map(Fetched::Object)
785            }
786        }
787    }
788}

790/// An input that is passed to the xref constructor so that we can fully resolve
791/// the PDF.
792#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone)]
793pub(crate) enum XRefInput<'a> {
794    /// This option is going to be uesd in 99.999% of the case. It contains the
795    /// raw data of the trailer dictionary which is then going to be processed.
796    TrailerDictData(&'a [u8]),
797    /// In case the trailer dictionary could not be read (for example because
798    /// it is cut-off), we just pass the object ID of the root dictionary
799    /// in case we have found one, and try our best to build the PDF just
800    /// with the information we have there.
801    ///
802    /// Note that this won't work if the document is encrypted, as we
803    /// can't access the crypto dictionary.
804    RootRef(ObjectIdentifier),
805}
806
807/// PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (43)) how far from the end of the file a `startxref` counts as
808/// the file's own footer, as `pdfcraft-cos` judges it (ISO 32000-2 §7.5.5 puts it on the last lines
809/// of the file).
810const STARTXREF_TAIL: usize = 4096;
811
812pub(crate) fn find_last_xref_pos(data: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
813    let needle = b"startxref";
814    let pos = findr_needle(data, needle)?;
815    let mut finder = Reader::new(data);
816    finder.jump(pos);
817    finder.forward_tag(needle)?;
818    finder.skip_white_spaces_and_comments();
819    finder.read_without_context::<i32>()?.try_into().ok()
820}
821
822/// PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (43)) whether the last update of the file was cut off before its
823/// own cross-reference section and trailer: the last `startxref` is not near the end of the file
824/// and objects follow it. That section would supersede the older ones (ISO 32000-2 §7.5.6), so
825/// the update's objects are the document; reading the older table the last `startxref` names
826/// shows a revision the document model (`pdfcraft-cos`, which rebuilds such a file from its
827/// object headers) does not have. A `startxref` near the end, or one followed only by other data
828/// (trailing junk), is no cut-off update.
829pub(crate) fn cut_off_update_follows(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
830    let needle = b"startxref";
831    findr_needle(data, needle).is_some_and(|pos| {
832        pos < data.len().saturating_sub(STARTXREF_TAIL) && data.get(pos.saturating_add(needle.len())..).is_some_and(has_object_header)
833    })
834}
835
836/// PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (43)) whether `data` holds an `N G obj` header: two runs of
837/// digits and the keyword, separated by white space, at the start of the data or after white
838/// space or `>`, the keyword ended by white space, a delimiter or the end of the data (ISO
839/// 32000-2 §7.2.3, Table 2), as the document model's repair scan reads it: `1 0 obj_name` is
840/// no header, and neither is one whose object number doesn't fit 32 bits (`4294967296 0 obj`),
841/// which that scan skips too. One linear pass, no allocation.
842fn has_object_header(data: &[u8]) -> bool {
843    let digits = |from: usize| data.get(from..).map_or(0, |rest| rest.iter().take_while(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()).count());
844    let spaces = |from: usize| data.get(from..).map_or(0, |rest| rest.iter().take_while(|&&b| is_white_space_character(b)).count());
845    let mut i = 0;
846    while i < data.len() {
847        let at_start = i.checked_sub(1).and_then(|prev| data.get(prev)).is_none_or(|&b| is_white_space_character(b) || b == b'>');
848        let n = if at_start { digits(i) } else { 0 };
849        if n == 0 {
850            i += 1;
851            continue;
852        }
853        let mut at = i + n;
854        let s1 = spaces(at);
855        at += s1;
856        let g = digits(at);
857        at += g;
858        let s2 = spaces(at);
859        at += s2;
860        // The object number as the model reads it, a 32-bit unsigned integer.
861        let number_fits = data.get(i..i + n).and_then(|d| core::str::from_utf8(d).ok()).is_some_and(|d| d.parse::<u32>().is_ok());
862        if number_fits
863            && s1 > 0
864            && g > 0
865            && s2 > 0
866            && data.get(at..).is_some_and(|rest| rest.starts_with(b"obj"))
867            && data
868                .get(at + 3)
869                .is_none_or(|&b| is_white_space_character(b) || matches!(b, b'(' | b')' | b'<' | b'>' | b'[' | b']' | b'{' | b'}' | b'/' | b'%'))
870        {
871            return true;
872        }
873        // Past the digits read: none of them starts a header.
874        i += n;
875    }
876    false
877}

879/// A type of xref entry.
880#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Copy)]
881enum EntryType {
882    /// An indirect object that is at a specific offset in the original data.
883    Normal(usize),
884    /// An indirect object that is part of an object stream. First number indicates the object
885    /// number of the _object stream_ (the generation number is always 0), the second number indicates
886    /// the index in the object stream.
887    ObjStream(u32, u32),
888}

933#[derive(Debug)]
934struct XRefEntry {
935    offset: usize,
936    gen_number: i32,
937    used: bool,
938}
939
940impl XRefEntry {
941    pub(crate) fn read(data: &[u8]) -> Option<Self> {
942        #[inline(always)]
943        fn parse_u32(data: &[u8]) -> Option<u32> {
944            let mut accum = 0_u32;
945
946            for byte in data {
947                accum = accum.checked_mul(10)?;
948
949                match *byte {
950                    b'0'..=b'9' => accum = accum.checked_add((*byte - b'0') as u32)?,
951                    _ => return None,
952                }
953            }
954
955            Some(accum)
956        }
957
958        let offset = parse_u32(&data[0..10])? as usize;
959        let gen_number = i32::try_from(parse_u32(&data[11..16])?).ok()?;
960
961        let used = data[17] == b'n';
962
963        Some(Self { offset, gen_number, used })
964    }
965}
966
967fn populate_xref_impl<'a>(data: &'a [u8], pos: usize, xref_map: &mut XrefMap) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
968    let mut visited = BTreeSet::new();
969    populate_xref_impl_inner(data, pos, xref_map, &mut visited)
970}
971
972/// The offset of the previous xref section (`Prev`).
973// PdfCraft patch: (#2366) some writers give `Prev` as a reference `N G R`. When this section's
974// own entries (`own`) place that object and it holds an offset (iText's `indirectPrev.pdf`), that
975// is the offset; otherwise its object number is (tiff2pdf, in JHOVE's PDF-HUL-157 files), as
976// `pdfcraft-cos` and other readers take it.
977fn prev_offset(data: &[u8], trailer: &Dict<'_>, own: &XrefMap) -> Option<usize> {
978    if let Some(prev) = trailer.get::<i32>(PREV) {
979        return usize::try_from(prev).ok();
980    }
981
982    let r = trailer.get_ref(PREV)?;
983    let id = ObjectIdentifier::new(r.obj_number, r.gen_number);
984    let held = match own.get(&id) {
985        Some(EntryType::Normal(at)) => {
986            let mut reader = Reader::new(data);
987            reader.jump(*at);
988            reader.read_with_context::<IndirectObject<i32>>(&ReaderContext::dummy()).filter(|o| o.id() == &id).map(|o| o.get()).filter(|p| *p >= 0)
989        }
990        _ => None,
991    };
992
993    usize::try_from(held.unwrap_or(r.obj_number)).ok()
994}
995
996/// Maximum number of allowed xref `Prev` pointers before we abort.
997const MAX_XREF_CHAIN_DEPTH: usize = 256;
998
999fn populate_xref_impl_inner<'a>(data: &'a [u8], pos: usize, xref_map: &mut XrefMap, visited: &mut BTreeSet<usize>) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
1000    if !visited.insert(pos) {
1001        warn!("circular xref PREV chain detected at offset {}", pos);
1002
1003        return None;
1004    }
1005
1006    if visited.len() > MAX_XREF_CHAIN_DEPTH {
1007        warn!("xref PREV chain exceeds maximum depth of {}", MAX_XREF_CHAIN_DEPTH);
1008
1009        return None;
1010    }
1011
1012    let mut reader = Reader::new(data);
1013    reader.jump(pos);
1014    // In case the position points to before the object number of a xref stream.
1015    reader.skip_white_spaces_and_comments();
1016
1017    let mut r2 = reader.clone();
1018    if reader.clone().read_without_context::<ObjectIdentifier>().is_some() {
1019        populate_from_xref_stream(data, &mut r2, xref_map, visited)
1020    } else {
1021        populate_from_xref_table(data, &mut r2, xref_map, visited)
1022    }
1023}
1024
1025pub(super) struct SubsectionHeader {
1026    pub(super) start: u32,
1027    pub(super) num_entries: u32,
1028}
1029
1030impl Readable<'_> for SubsectionHeader {
1031    fn read(r: &mut Reader<'_>, _: &ReaderContext<'_>) -> Option<Self> {
1032        r.skip_white_spaces();
1033        let start = r.read_without_context::<u32>()?;
1034        r.skip_white_spaces();
1035        let num_entries = r.read_without_context::<u32>()?;
1036        r.skip_white_spaces();
1037
1038        Some(Self { start, num_entries })
1039    }
1040}
1041
1042/// Populate the xref table, and return the trailer dict.
1043fn populate_from_xref_table<'a>(
1044    data: &'a [u8],
1045    reader: &mut Reader<'a>,
1046    insert_map: &mut XrefMap,
1047    visited: &mut BTreeSet<usize>,
1048) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
1049    let trailer = {
1050        let mut reader = reader.clone();
1051        read_xref_table_trailer(&mut reader, &ReaderContext::dummy())?
1052    };
1053
1054    reader.skip_white_spaces();
1055    reader.forward_tag(b"xref")?;
1056    reader.skip_white_spaces();
1057
1058    let mut max_obj = 0;
1059    // PdfCraft patch: (#2366) this section's entries are read first, for `prev_offset`.
1060    let mut own = XrefMap::default();
1061
1062    while let Some(header) = reader.read_without_context::<SubsectionHeader>() {
1063        reader.skip_white_spaces();
1064
1065        let start = header.start;
1066        let end = start.checked_add(header.num_entries)?;
1067
1068        for obj_number in start..end {
1069            max_obj = max(max_obj, obj_number);
1070            let bytes = reader.read_bytes(XREF_ENTRY_LEN)?;
1071            let entry = XRefEntry::read(bytes)?;
1072
1073            // Specification says we should ignore any object number > SIZE, but probably
1074            // not important?
1075            if entry.used {
1076                own.insert(ObjectIdentifier::new(obj_number as i32, entry.gen_number), EntryType::Normal(entry.offset));
1077            }
1078        }
1079    }
1080
1081    if let Some(prev) = prev_offset(data, &trailer, &own) {
1082        // First insert the entries from any previous xref tables.
1083        populate_xref_impl_inner(data, prev, insert_map, visited)?;
1084    }
1085
1086    // In hybrid files, entries in `XRefStm` should have higher priority, therefore we insert them
1087    // after looking at `PREV`.
1088    if let Some(xref_stm) = trailer.get::<i32>(XREF_STM) {
1089        populate_xref_impl_inner(data, xref_stm as usize, insert_map, visited)?;
1090    }
1091
1092    insert_map.extend(own);
1093
1094    Some(trailer.data())
1095}
1096
1097fn populate_from_xref_stream<'a>(
1098    data: &'a [u8],
1099    reader: &mut Reader<'a>,
1100    insert_map: &mut XrefMap,
1101    visited: &mut BTreeSet<usize>,
1102) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
1103    let stream = reader.read_with_context::<IndirectObject<Stream<'_>>>(&ReaderContext::dummy())?.get();
1104
1105    let size = stream.dict().get::<u32>(SIZE)?;
1106
1107    let [f1_len, f2_len, f3_len] = stream.dict().get::<[u8; 3]>(W)?;
1108
1109    // PdfCraft patch: the type field is read at its full width, so it is bounded like the offset.
1110    if f1_len > size_of::<u64>() as u8 || f2_len > size_of::<u64>() as u8 {
1111        error!("xref field length is larger than the allowed limit");
1112
1113        return None;
1114    }
1115
1116    let xref_data = stream.decoded().ok()?;
1117    // PdfCraft patch: (#2366) this section's entries are read first, for `prev_offset`.
1118    let mut own = XrefMap::default();
1119    let mut xref_reader = Reader::new(xref_data.as_ref());
1120
1121    if let Some(arr) = stream.dict().get::<Array<'_>>(INDEX) {
1122        let iter = arr.iter::<(u32, u32)>();
1123
1124        for (start, num_elements) in iter {
1125            xref_stream_subsection(&mut xref_reader, start, num_elements, f1_len, f2_len, f3_len, &mut own)?;
1126        }
1127    } else {
1128        xref_stream_subsection(&mut xref_reader, 0, size, f1_len, f2_len, f3_len, &mut own)?;
1129    }
1130
1131    if let Some(prev) = prev_offset(data, stream.dict(), &own) {
1132        // First insert the entries from any previous xref tables.
1133        let _ = populate_xref_impl_inner(data, prev, insert_map, visited)?;
1134    }
1135
1136    insert_map.extend(own);
1137
1138    Some(stream.dict().data())
1139}
1140
1141fn xref_stream_num(data: &[u8]) -> Option<u32> {
1142    Some(match data.len() {
1143        0 => return None,
1144        1 => u8::from_be(data[0]) as u32,
1145        2 => u16::from_be_bytes(data[0..2].try_into().ok()?) as u32,
1146        3 => u32::from_be_bytes([0, data[0], data[1], data[2]]),
1147        4 => u32::from_be_bytes(data[0..4].try_into().ok()?),
1148        8 => {
1149            if let Ok(num) = u32::try_from(u64::from_be_bytes(data[0..8].try_into().ok()?)) {
1150                return Some(num);
1151            } else {
1152                warn!("xref stream number is too large");
1153
1154                return None;
1155            }
1156        }
1157        _n => {
1158            warn!("invalid xref stream number {_n}");
1159
1160            return None;
1161        }
1162    })
1163}
1164
1165fn xref_stream_subsection<'a>(
1166    xref_reader: &mut Reader<'a>,
1167    start: u32,
1168    num_elements: u32,
1169    f1_len: u8,
1170    f2_len: u8,
1171    f3_len: u8,
1172    insert_map: &mut XrefMap,
1173) -> Option<()> {
1174    // PdfCraft patch: every entry must be backed by stream bytes. With all widths zero an entry
1175    // reads nothing, so a tiny stream could declare billions of entries; and a count past the
1176    // decoded data is refused before any of it is inserted.
1177    let width = f1_len as usize + f2_len as usize + f3_len as usize;
1178    if width == 0 {
1179        warn!("xref stream entries have no width");
1180
1181        return None;
1182    }
1183    let available = xref_reader.len().saturating_sub(xref_reader.offset());
1184    if (num_elements as usize).checked_mul(width).is_none_or(|need| need > available) {
1185        warn!("xref stream subsection declares more entries than its data holds");
1186
1187        return None;
1188    }
1189
1190    for i in 0..num_elements {
1191        // A zero-width type field defaults to 1 (ISO 32000-2 §7.5.8.2, `/W`).
1192        let f_type = if f1_len == 0 {
1193            1
1194        } else {
1195            // PdfCraft patch: the type field is read big-endian at its full `/W[0]` width.
1196            let bytes = xref_reader.read_bytes(f1_len as usize)?;
1197            bytes.iter().fold(0u64, |acc, b| (acc << 8) | u64::from(*b))
1198        };
1199
1200        // PdfCraft patch: object numbers are stored as `i32`; a subsection running past
1201        // `i32::MAX` is refused instead of overflowing or turning negative.
1202        let obj_number = i32::try_from(start.checked_add(i)?).ok()?;
1203
1204        match f_type {
1205            // We don't care about free objects.
1206            0 => {
1207                xref_reader.skip_bytes(f2_len as usize + f3_len as usize)?;
1208            }
1209            1 => {
1210                let offset = if f2_len > 0 {
1211                    let data = xref_reader.read_bytes(f2_len as usize)?;
1212                    xref_stream_num(data)?
1213                } else {
1214                    0
1215                };
1216
1217                let gen_number = if f3_len > 0 {
1218                    let data = xref_reader.read_bytes(f3_len as usize)?;
1219                    xref_stream_num(data)?
1220                } else {
1221                    0
1222                };
1223
1224                insert_map.insert(ObjectIdentifier::new(obj_number, gen_number as i32), EntryType::Normal(offset as usize));
1225            }
1226            2 => {
1227                let obj_stream_number = {
1228                    let data = xref_reader.read_bytes(f2_len as usize)?;
1229                    xref_stream_num(data)?
1230                };
1231                let gen_number = 0;
1232                let index = if f3_len > 0 {
1233                    let data = xref_reader.read_bytes(f3_len as usize)?;
1234                    xref_stream_num(data)?
1235                } else {
1236                    0
1237                };
1238
1239                insert_map.insert(ObjectIdentifier::new(obj_number, gen_number), EntryType::ObjStream(obj_stream_number, index));
1240            }
1241            _ => {
1242                warn!("xref has unknown field type {f_type}");
1243
1244                return None;
1245            }
1246        }
1247    }
1248
1249    Some(())
1250}
1251
1252fn read_xref_table_trailer<'a>(reader: &mut Reader<'a>, ctx: &ReaderContext<'a>) -> Option<Dict<'a>> {
1253    reader.skip_white_spaces();
1254    reader.forward_tag(b"xref")?;
1255    reader.skip_white_spaces();
1256
1257    while let Some(header) = reader.read_without_context::<SubsectionHeader>() {
1258        let len = XREF_ENTRY_LEN.checked_mul(header.num_entries as usize)?;
1259        reader.jump(reader.offset().checked_add(len)?);
1260    }
1261
1262    reader.skip_white_spaces();
1263    reader.forward_tag(b"trailer")?;
1264    reader.skip_white_spaces();
1265
1266    reader.read_with_context::<Dict<'_>>(ctx)
1267}
1268
1269fn get_decryptor(trailer_dict: &Dict<'_>, password: &[u8]) -> Result<Decryptor, XRefError> {
1270    if let Some(encryption_dict) = trailer_dict.get::<Dict<'_>>(ENCRYPT) {
1271        let id = if let Some(id) = trailer_dict.get::<Array<'_>>(ID).and_then(|a| a.flex_iter().next::<object::String<'_>>()) {
1272            id.to_vec()
1273        } else {
1274            // Assume an empty ID entry.
1275            vec![]
1276        };
1277
1278        get(&encryption_dict, &id, password).map_err(XRefError::Encryption)
1279    } else {
1280        Ok(Decryptor::None)
1281    }
1282}
1283
1284/// PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (22)) each object stream's parsed `(object number, offset)`
1285/// pairs ([`read_object_stream_index`]) by the stream's identifier, `None` for pairs that don't
1286/// parse. Never cleared, like the decoded stream data they index (`Data`), which a repair keeps
1287/// too. Bounded by that data: every pair takes at least three of its bytes.
1288type ObjectStreamIndexes = FxHashMap<ObjectIdentifier, Option<Arc<Vec<(u32, usize)>>>>;
1289
1290/// The `(object number, offset)` pairs at the start of an object stream's decoded `data`, the
1291/// offsets measured from the start of `data`. `None` when the pairs don't parse. Reads no
1292/// further than the data holds, whatever `/N` claims.
1293fn read_object_stream_index(num_objects: usize, first_offset: usize, data: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<(u32, usize)>> {
1294    let mut r = Reader::new(data);
1295
1296    let mut offsets = vec![];
1297
1298    for _ in 0..num_objects {
1299        r.skip_white_spaces_and_comments();
1300        // Skip object number
1301        let obj_num = r.read_without_context::<u32>()?;
1302        r.skip_white_spaces_and_comments();
1303        let relative_offset = r.read_without_context::<usize>()?;
1304        // PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (22)) an offset past `usize` is malformed (it wrapped).
1305        offsets.push((obj_num, first_offset.checked_add(relative_offset)?));
1306    }
1307
1308    Some(offsets)
1309}
1310
1311struct ObjectStream<'a> {
1312    data: &'a [u8],
1313    ctx: ReaderContext<'a>,
1314    offsets: Arc<Vec<(u32, usize)>>,
1315}
1316
1317impl<'a> ObjectStream<'a> {
1318    fn new(inner: Stream<'_>, data: &'a [u8], ctx: &ReaderContext<'a>) -> Option<Self> {
1319        let num_objects = inner.dict().get::<usize>(N)?;
1320        let first_offset = inner.dict().get::<usize>(FIRST)?;
1321        let offsets = read_object_stream_index(num_objects, first_offset, data)?;
1322
1323        Some(Self::with_offsets(data, ctx, Arc::new(offsets)))
1324    }
1325
1326    /// PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (22)) an object stream whose index is already parsed.
1327    fn with_offsets(data: &'a [u8], ctx: &ReaderContext<'a>, offsets: Arc<Vec<(u32, usize)>>) -> Self {
1328        let mut ctx = ctx.clone();
1329        ctx.set_in_object_stream(true);
1330
1331        Self { data, ctx, offsets }
1332    }
1333
1334    fn get<T>(&self, index: u32) -> Option<T>
1335    where
1336        T: ObjectLike<'a>,
1337    {
1338        let offset = self.offsets.get(index as usize)?.1;
1339        let mut r = Reader::new(self.data);
1340        r.jump(offset);
1341        r.skip_white_spaces_and_comments();
1342
1343        r.read_with_context::<T>(&self.ctx)
1344    }
1345
1346    /// PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (33)) what the object at `index` refers to, when a reference is
1347    /// all it holds.
1348    fn reference(&self, index: u32) -> Option<ObjectIdentifier> {
1349        let offset = self.offsets.get(index as usize)?.1;
1350        let mut r = Reader::new(self.data);
1351        r.jump(offset);
1352        r.skip_white_spaces_and_comments();
1353
1354        Some(r.read_without_context::<ObjRef>()?.into())
1355    }
1356}
1357
1358/// PdfCraft patch: (hayro-syntax (33)) what the indirect object `id` at `r` refers to, when a
1359/// reference is all it holds.
1360fn held_reference(mut r: Reader<'_>, id: ObjectIdentifier) -> Option<ObjectIdentifier> {
1361    if r.read_without_context::<ObjectIdentifier>()? != id {
1362        return None;
1363    }
1364    r.skip_white_spaces_and_comments();
1365
1366    Some(r.read_without_context::<ObjRef>()?.into())
1367}

1369fn parse_metadata(info_dict: &Dict<'_>) -> Metadata {
1370    Metadata {
1371        creation_date: info_dict.get::<object::String<'_>>(CREATION_DATE).and_then(|c| DateTime::from_bytes(&c)),
1372        modification_date: info_dict.get::<object::String<'_>>(MOD_DATE).and_then(|c| DateTime::from_bytes(&c)),
1373        title: info_dict.get::<object::String<'_>>(TITLE).map(|t| t.to_vec()),
1374        author: info_dict.get::<object::String<'_>>(AUTHOR).map(|t| t.to_vec()),
1375        subject: info_dict.get::<object::String<'_>>(SUBJECT).map(|t| t.to_vec()),
1376        keywords: info_dict.get::<object::String<'_>>(KEYWORDS).map(|t| t.to_vec()),
1377        creator: info_dict.get::<object::String<'_>>(CREATOR).map(|t| t.to_vec()),
1378        producer: info_dict.get::<object::String<'_>>(PRODUCER).map(|t| t.to_vec()),
1379    }
1380}

1382#[cfg(any())]
1383mod tests {
1384    use super::*;
1385    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::Pdf;
1386
1387    /// A file with an xref stream: `stored` are objects on their own, as they would follow
1388    /// `n 0 obj`, and `packed` says of each object in an object stream which stream and place.
1389    fn with_xref_stream(stored: &[(u32, Vec<u8>)], packed: &[(u32, u32, u16)]) -> Vec<u8> {
1390        let mut out = b"%PDF-1.7\n".to_vec();
1391        let mut offsets = alloc::collections::BTreeMap::new();
1392        for (num, body) in stored {
1393            offsets.insert(*num, out.len());
1394            out.extend_from_slice(alloc::format!("{num} 0 obj ").as_bytes());
1395            out.extend_from_slice(body);
1396            out.extend_from_slice(b"\nendobj\n");
1397        }
1398        let last = stored.iter().map(|o| o.0).chain(packed.iter().map(|o| o.0)).max().unwrap_or(0);
1399        let (xref, size) = (last + 1, last + 2);
1400        let at = out.len();
1401        offsets.insert(xref, at);
1402        let packed: alloc::collections::BTreeMap<u32, (u32, u16)> = packed.iter().map(|o| (o.0, (o.1, o.2))).collect();
1403        let mut rows = Vec::new();
1404        for num in 0..size {
1405            if let Some(offset) = offsets.get(&num) {
1406                rows.push(1);
1407                rows.extend_from_slice(&(*offset as u32).to_be_bytes());
1408                rows.extend_from_slice(&[0, 0]);
1409            } else if let Some((stream, index)) = packed.get(&num) {
1410                rows.push(2);
1411                rows.extend_from_slice(&stream.to_be_bytes());
1412                rows.extend_from_slice(&index.to_be_bytes());
1413            } else {
1414                rows.extend_from_slice(&[0; 7]);
1415            }
1416        }
1417        out.extend_from_slice(
1418            alloc::format!("{xref} 0 obj << /Type /XRef /Size {size} /W [1 4 2] /Root 1 0 R /Length {} >> stream\n", rows.len()).as_bytes(),
1419        );
1420        out.extend_from_slice(&rows);
1421        out.extend_from_slice(alloc::format!("\nendstream endobj\nstartxref\n{at}\n%%EOF\n").as_bytes());
1422        out
1423    }
1424
1425    /// `/Type /ObjStm` around `members`, each stored at its offset, and `entries` of its own.
1426    fn object_stream_of(members: &[(u32, &[u8])], entries: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
1427        let (mut head, mut body) = (alloc::string::String::new(), Vec::new());
1428        for (num, member) in members {
1429            head.push_str(&alloc::format!("{num} {} ", body.len()));
1430            body.extend_from_slice(member);
1431            body.push(b'\n');
1432        }
1433        head.push('\n');
1434        let dict =
1435            alloc::format!("<< /Type /ObjStm /N {} /First {} /Length {} {entries} >> stream\n", members.len(), head.len(), head.len() + body.len());
1436        let mut out = dict.into_bytes();
1437        out.extend_from_slice(head.as_bytes());
1438        out.extend_from_slice(&body);
1439        out.extend_from_slice(b"\nendstream");
1440        out
1441    }
1442
1443    fn page_objects() -> Vec<(u32, Vec<u8>)> {
1444        vec![
1445            (1, b"<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>".to_vec()),
1446            (2, b"<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>".to_vec()),
1447            (3, b"<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 10 10] >>".to_vec()),
1448        ]
1449    }
1450
1451    /// An object stream is a stream stored as that object, however many references lead to one.
1452    /// Object 10 holds a reference to 11, a stream stored inside object stream 12, and 31 claims to
1453    /// be in 10, with 11's `/N`, `/First` or `/Length` being 31: reading it recursed until the
1454    /// stack ran out. It reads as missing, and so does a member of such a stream.
1455    #[cfg(any())]
1456    fn an_object_stream_isnt_reached_through_a_reference() {
1457        for key in ["N", "First", "Length"] {
1458            let inner = alloc::format!("<< /Type /ObjStm /{key} 31 0 R >> stream\n31 0 1\n\nendstream");
1459            let mut stored = page_objects();
1460            stored.push((10, b"11 0 R".to_vec()));
1461            stored.push((12, object_stream_of(&[(11, inner.as_bytes())], "")));
1462            let pdf = Pdf::new(with_xref_stream(&stored, &[(11, 12, 0), (31, 10, 0)])).unwrap();
1463            assert_eq!(pdf.xref().get::<i32>(ObjectIdentifier::new(31, 0)), None, "{key}");
1464        }
1465        let inner = b"<< /Type /ObjStm /N 1 /First 5 /Length 8 >> stream\n20 0 7\n\nendstream";
1466        let mut stored = page_objects();
1467        stored.push((10, b"11 0 R".to_vec()));
1468        stored.push((12, object_stream_of(&[(11, inner)], "")));
1469        let pdf = Pdf::new(with_xref_stream(&stored, &[(11, 12, 0), (20, 10, 0)])).unwrap();
1470        assert_eq!(pdf.xref().get::<i32>(ObjectIdentifier::new(20, 0)), None);
1471    }
1472
1473    /// `count` object streams stored as themselves, the `keys` of each a member of the next, or
1474    /// with `ring` of the first after the last. Reading the first member reads them all, and it is
1475    /// `count + 100` to tell.
1476    fn chain_of_object_streams(count: u32, keys: &[&str], ring: bool) -> Vec<u8> {
1477        let mut stored = page_objects();
1478        let mut packed = Vec::new();
1479        for i in 0..count {
1480            let (stream, member) = (100 + 2 * i, 101 + 2 * i);
1481            let value = if i == 0 { count + 100 } else { 1 };
1482            let data = alloc::format!("{member} 0 \n{value}\n");
1483            let (first, length) = (alloc::format!("{}", alloc::format!("{member} 0 \n").len()), alloc::format!("{}", data.len()));
1484            let next = match (i + 1 == count, ring) {
1485                (true, true) => "101 0 R".into(),
1486                (true, false) => "1".into(),
1487                _ => alloc::format!("{} 0 R", member + 2),
1488            };
1489            let entry = |key, own: &'_ str| if keys.contains(&key) { next.clone() } else { own.into() };
1490            let (n, first, length): (alloc::string::String, alloc::string::String, alloc::string::String) =
1491                (entry("N", "1"), entry("First", &first), entry("Length", &length));
1492            let body = alloc::format!("<< /Type /ObjStm /N {n} /First {first} /Length {length} >> stream\n{data}\nendstream");
1493            stored.push((stream, body.into_bytes()));
1494            packed.push((member, stream, 0));
1495        }
1496        with_xref_stream(&stored, &packed)
1497    }
1498
1499    /// A chain of object streams, each with a member of the next for its `/N`, `/First` or
1500    /// `/Length`, had no limit: one read recursed through all of them, holding a copy of the chain
1501    /// at each, and 50,000 ran out of an 8 MiB stack. It stops at the gate's limit, on half the stack
1502    /// of a render worker. Past that `/N` and `/First` can't be read, so the member reads as missing,
1503    /// and a `/Length` that can't be read falls back on `endstream`, so it reads. A short chain reads.
1504    #[cfg(any())]
1505    fn a_chain_of_object_streams_ends_at_the_limit_of_nested_loads() {
1506        for key in ["N", "First", "Length"] {
1507            let pdf = chain_of_object_streams(50_000, &[key], false);
1508            std::thread::Builder::new()
1509                .stack_size(1 << 20)
1510                .spawn(move || {
1511                    let pdf = Pdf::new(pdf).unwrap();
1512                    let read = pdf.xref().get::<i32>(ObjectIdentifier::new(101, 0));
1513                    assert_eq!(read, (key == "Length").then_some(50_100), "{key}");
1514                })
1515                .unwrap()
1516                .join()
1517                .unwrap();
1518        }
1519        let pdf = Pdf::new(chain_of_object_streams(10, &["N"], false)).unwrap();
1520        assert_eq!(pdf.xref().get::<i32>(ObjectIdentifier::new(101, 0)), Some(110));
1521    }
1522
1523    /// `/Length` and `/N` or `/First` both by reference were two ways to the next stream's index,
1524    /// and an index that fails isn't remembered, so the work doubled at each stream: 65 streams, one
1525    /// past the limit, in 8 KB, didn't finish, and other threads waited at the gate. The index reads
1526    /// the dictionary alone now. Without that this doesn't end, so the time allowed can't fail it.
1527    #[cfg(any())]
1528    fn a_chain_of_object_streams_takes_no_more_work_for_two_ways_on() {
1529        for (count, ring) in [(65, false), (20, true), (5_000, false)] {
1530            for keys in [&["Length", "N"][..], &["Length", "First"]] {
1531                let pdf = chain_of_object_streams(count, keys, ring);
1532                let (done, finished) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
1533                std::thread::Builder::new()
1534                    .stack_size(1 << 20)
1535                    .spawn(move || {
1536                        let pdf = Pdf::new(pdf).unwrap();
1537                        let _ = pdf.xref().get::<i32>(ObjectIdentifier::new(101, 0));
1538                        let _ = done.send(());
1539                    })
1540                    .unwrap();
1541                assert!(finished.recv_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(120)).is_ok(), "{keys:?} of {count}");
1542            }
1543        }
1544    }
1545
1546    /// Object 5, a member of a real object stream, holds a reference to object 6 stored on its own,
1547    /// and 7, stored on its own, to 8, a member: each reads as what it names.
1548    #[cfg(any())]
1549    fn a_reference_held_in_either_storage_is_followed() {
1550        let mut stored = page_objects();
1551        stored.push((6, b"42".to_vec()));
1552        stored.push((7, b"8 0 R".to_vec()));
1553        stored.push((9, object_stream_of(&[(5, b"6 0 R"), (8, b"43")], "")));
1554        let pdf = Pdf::new(with_xref_stream(&stored, &[(5, 9, 0), (8, 9, 1)])).unwrap();
1555        assert_eq!(pdf.xref().get::<i32>(ObjectIdentifier::new(5, 0)), Some(42));
1556        assert_eq!(pdf.xref().get::<i32>(ObjectIdentifier::new(7, 0)), Some(43));
1557    }
1558
1559    /// With no page tree, every page object is a page, and one that another object only refers to
1560    /// is one page, not two.
1561    #[cfg(any())]
1562    fn a_page_a_reference_is_held_to_is_found_once() {
1563        let mut stored = page_objects();
1564        stored[0].1 = b"<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 99 0 R >>".to_vec();
1565        stored[2].1 = b"<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 10 10] /Contents 4 0 R >>".to_vec();
1566        stored.push((4, b"<< /Length 0 >> stream\n\nendstream".to_vec()));
1567        stored.push((12, b"3 0 R".to_vec()));
1568        let pdf = Pdf::new(with_xref_stream(&stored, &[])).unwrap();
1569        assert_eq!(pdf.pages().len(), 1);
1570    }

1572    // PdfCraft patch tests (ported from craft-libs): xref stream entries are bounded by the
1573    // decoded data, and the type field is read at its full width.
1574    #[cfg(any())]
1575    fn xref_stream_entries_need_backing_bytes() {
1576        let mut map = XrefMap::default();
1577        // All widths zero: an entry reads nothing, so none may be declared.
1578        let mut empty = Reader::new(&[]);
1579        assert!(xref_stream_subsection(&mut empty, 0, u32::MAX, 0, 0, 0, &mut map).is_none());
1580        assert!(map.is_empty());
1581        // Three entries of width 3 need nine bytes; eight are refused before any insert.
1582        let data = [1, 0, 9, 1, 0, 9, 1, 0];
1583        let mut short = Reader::new(&data);
1584        assert!(xref_stream_subsection(&mut short, 0, 3, 1, 1, 1, &mut map).is_none());
1585        assert!(map.is_empty());
1586        let mut whole = Reader::new(&data[..6]);
1587        assert!(xref_stream_subsection(&mut whole, 0, 2, 1, 1, 1, &mut map).is_some());
1588        assert_eq!(map.len(), 2);
1589        // A subsection running past object number i32::MAX is refused.
1590        for start in [i32::MAX as u32, u32::MAX] {
1591            let mut past_end = XrefMap::default();
1592            let mut wrap = Reader::new(&data[..6]);
1593            assert!(xref_stream_subsection(&mut wrap, start, 2, 1, 1, 1, &mut past_end).is_none());
1594            assert!(past_end.keys().all(|id| id.obj_number >= 0));
1595        }
1596    }

1598    #[cfg(any())]
1599    fn xref_stream_type_field_uses_the_full_w0_width() {
1600        // /W [2 1 1]: two-byte type 0x0001 (normal), offset 7, gen 0.
1601        let mut map = XrefMap::default();
1602        let mut reader = Reader::new(&[0u8, 1, 7, 0]);
1603        assert!(xref_stream_subsection(&mut reader, 5, 1, 2, 1, 1, &mut map).is_some());
1604        assert!(matches!(map.get(&ObjectIdentifier::new(5, 0)), Some(EntryType::Normal(7))));
1605    }

1607    #[cfg(any())]
1608    fn xref_stream_loader_rejects_oversized_w0() {
1609        // One normal entry (offset 7, gen 0) whose type field is `type_len` bytes wide, so only
1610        // the width of /W[0] differs between the two streams.
1611        let load = |type_len: usize| {
1612            let mut entry = vec![0u8; type_len];
1613            entry[type_len - 1] = 1;
1614            entry.extend_from_slice(&[7, 0]);
1615            let mut data =
1616                format!("1 0 obj\n<< /Type /XRef /Size 6 /Index [5 1] /W [{type_len} 1 1] /Length {} >>\nstream\n", entry.len()).into_bytes();
1617            data.extend_from_slice(&entry);
1618            data.extend_from_slice(b"\nendstream\nendobj\n");
1619            let mut map = XrefMap::default();
1620            let got = populate_from_xref_stream(&data, &mut Reader::new(&data), &mut map, &mut BTreeSet::new());
1621            got.is_some()
1622        };
1623        assert!(load(8));
1624        assert!(!load(9));
1625    }

1627    // Contributor-original, MIT OR Apache-2.0. Matches the bounded, uncompressed
1628    // synthetic regression used to reproduce the cold-publication race. A second
1629    // stream optionally checks that racing registration never aliases two ids.
1630    fn object_stream_fixture(second: bool) -> Vec<u8> {
1631        let mut out = b"%PDF-1.5\n".to_vec();
1632        let mut offsets = alloc::collections::BTreeMap::new();
1633        fn object(out: &mut Vec<u8>, offsets: &mut alloc::collections::BTreeMap<u32, usize>, n: u32, body: &[u8]) {
1634            offsets.insert(n, out.len());
1635            out.extend_from_slice(format!("{n} 0 obj\n").as_bytes());
1636            out.extend_from_slice(body);
1637            out.extend_from_slice(b"\nendobj\n");
1638        }
1639        object(&mut out, &mut offsets, 1, b"<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>");
1640        object(&mut out, &mut offsets, 2, b"<< /Type /Pages /Count 1 /Kids [3 0 R] >>");
1641        object(&mut out, &mut offsets, 3, b"<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 100 100] >>");
1642        let mut payload = b"20 0 << /Marker 123 >>".to_vec();
1643        payload.resize(payload.len() + 4 * 1024 * 1024, b' ');
1644        let mut stream = format!("<< /Type /ObjStm /N 1 /First 5 /Length {} >>\nstream\n", payload.len()).into_bytes();
1645        stream.extend(payload);
1646        stream.extend_from_slice(b"\nendstream");
1647        object(&mut out, &mut offsets, 10, &stream);
1648        if second {
1649            let payload = b"21 0 << /Marker 456 >>";
1650            let mut stream = format!("<< /Type /ObjStm /N 1 /First 5 /Length {} >>\nstream\n", payload.len()).into_bytes();
1651            stream.extend_from_slice(payload);
1652            stream.extend_from_slice(b"\nendstream");
1653            object(&mut out, &mut offsets, 12, &stream);
1654        }
1655        let xref = out.len();
1656        offsets.insert(11, xref);
1657        let size = if second { 22 } else { 21 };
1658        let mut rows = Vec::new();
1659        for number in 0..size {
1660            let (kind, a, b): (u8, u32, u16) = match number {
1661                20 => (2, 10, 0),
1662                21 => (2, 12, 0),
1663                n => offsets.get(&n).map_or((0, 0, 65535), |offset| (1, *offset as u32, 0)),
1664            };
1665            rows.push(kind);
1666            rows.extend_from_slice(&a.to_be_bytes());
1667            rows.extend_from_slice(&b.to_be_bytes());
1668        }
1669        let mut stream = format!("<< /Type /XRef /Size {size} /Root 1 0 R /W [1 4 2] /Length {} >>\nstream\n", rows.len()).into_bytes();
1670        stream.extend(rows);
1671        stream.extend_from_slice(b"\nendstream");
1672        object(&mut out, &mut offsets, 11, &stream);
1673        out.extend_from_slice(format!("startxref\n{xref}\n%%EOF\n").as_bytes());
1674        out
1675    }

1677    #[cfg(any())]
1678    fn concurrent_cold_object_stream_reads_all_succeed() {
1679        use std::sync::Barrier;
1680        let bytes = Arc::new(object_stream_fixture(true));
1681        for _ in 0..10 {
1682            let pdf = Arc::new(crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::Pdf::new(bytes.clone()).unwrap());
1683            let barrier = Arc::new(Barrier::new(16));
1684            let jobs: Vec<_> = (0..16)
1685                .map(|_| {
1686                    let (pdf, barrier) = (pdf.clone(), barrier.clone());
1687                    std::thread::spawn(move || {
1688                        barrier.wait();
1689                        for (id, marker) in [(20, 123), (21, 456), (20, 123)] {
1690                            let dict = pdf.xref().get::<Dict<'_>>(ObjectIdentifier::new(id, 0)).unwrap();
1691                            assert_eq!(dict.get::<i32>(b"Marker"), Some(marker));
1692                        }
1693                    })
1694                })
1695                .collect();
1696            for job in jobs {
1697                job.join().unwrap();
1698            }
1699        }
1700    }

1703    fn an_object_stream_and_its_first_member_are_both_enumerated() {
1704        // Both sit at (stream offset, 0) in `objects`' ordering; one object per location must
1705        // not cost either of them.
1706        let pdf = crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::Pdf::new(object_stream_fixture(false)).unwrap();
1707        let objects: Vec<_> = pdf.xref().objects().into_iter().collect();
1708        assert!(objects.iter().any(|o| matches!(o, Object::Stream(_))));
1709        assert!(objects.iter().any(|o| matches!(o, Object::Dict(d) if d.get::<i32>(b"Marker") == Some(123))));

1726    #[cfg(any())]
1727    fn concurrent_repair_and_read_retries_the_repaired_map() {
1728        let pdf = Arc::new(crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::Pdf::new(object_stream_fixture(false)).unwrap());
1729        let Inner::Some(repr) = &pdf.xref().0 else { panic!("real xref") };
1730        repr.map.put().xref_map.insert(ObjectIdentifier::new(1, 0), EntryType::Normal(0));
1731        let barrier = Arc::new(std::sync::Barrier::new(16));
1732        let jobs: Vec<_> = (0..16)
1733            .map(|_| {
1734                let (pdf, barrier) = (pdf.clone(), barrier.clone());
1735                std::thread::spawn(move || {
1736                    barrier.wait();
1737                    for _ in 0..8 {
1738                        let root = pdf.xref().get::<Dict<'_>>(ObjectIdentifier::new(1, 0)).unwrap();
1739                        assert!(root.get_ref(PAGES).is_some());
1740                        pdf.xref().repair(); // already repaired is an idempotent no-op
1741                    }
1742                })
1743            })
1744            .collect();
1745        for job in jobs {
1746            job.join().unwrap();
1747        }
1748        assert!(repr.map.get().repaired);

1751    #[cfg(any())]
1752    fn poisoned_repair_lock_does_not_cascade_or_retry_repair() {
1753        use std::panic::{AssertUnwindSafe, catch_unwind};
1754        let pdf = crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::Pdf::new(object_stream_fixture(false)).unwrap();
1755        let Inner::Some(repr) = &pdf.xref().0 else { panic!("real xref") };
1756        assert!(
1757            catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
1758                let mut map = repr.map.put();
1759                map.repaired = true; // same state as an unwinding fallback before publication
1760                panic!("injected repair failure");
1761            }))
1762            .is_err()
1763        );
1764        pdf.xref().repair();
1765        assert!(pdf.xref().get::<Dict<'_>>(ObjectIdentifier::new(1, 0)).is_some());
1766        assert!(repr.map.get().repaired);
1767    }

1789    #[cfg(any())]
1790    fn prev_as_reference_reaches_the_earlier_section() {
1791        let mut pdf = b"%PDF-1.0\n1 0 obj\n<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>\nendobj\n".to_vec();
1792        let first_xref_pos = pdf.len();
1793        pdf.extend_from_slice(
1794            format!(
1795                "xref\n\
1796                 0 2\n\
1797                 0000000000 65535 f \n\
1798                 0000000009 00000 n \n\
1799                 trailer\n<< /Size 2 /Root 1 0 R >>\n\
1800                 startxref\n{first_xref_pos}\n%%EOF\n"
1801            )
1802            .as_bytes(),
1803        );
1804        let second_xref_pos = pdf.len();
1805        pdf.extend_from_slice(
1806            format!(
1807                "xref\n\
1808                 0 1\n\
1809                 0000000000 65535 f \n\
1810                 trailer\n<< /Size 2 /Root 1 0 R /Prev {first_xref_pos} 0 R >>\n\
1811                 startxref\n{second_xref_pos}\n%%EOF"
1812            )
1813            .as_bytes(),
1814        );
1815
1816        let mut xref_map = FxHashMap::default();
1817        let xref_pos = find_last_xref_pos(pdf.as_ref()).unwrap();
1818        assert_eq!(xref_pos, second_xref_pos);
1819        populate_xref_impl(pdf.as_ref(), xref_pos, &mut xref_map).unwrap();
1820        assert!(xref_map.contains_key(&ObjectIdentifier::new(1, 0)));
1821    }

1823    #[cfg(any())]
1824    fn prev_as_reference_to_an_object_holding_the_offset_reads_that_offset() {
1825        let mut pdf = b"%PDF-1.0\n1 0 obj\n<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>\nendobj\n".to_vec();
1826        let first_xref_pos = pdf.len();
1827        pdf.extend_from_slice(
1828            format!(
1829                "xref\n\
1830                 0 2\n\
1831                 0000000000 65535 f \n\
1832                 0000000009 00000 n \n\
1833                 trailer\n<< /Size 2 /Root 1 0 R >>\n\
1834                 startxref\n{first_xref_pos}\n%%EOF\n"
1835            )
1836            .as_bytes(),
1837        );
1838        // Object 3 holds the offset; read as offset 3, `Prev` would point inside the header.
1839        let held_pos = pdf.len();
1840        pdf.extend_from_slice(format!("3 0 obj\n{first_xref_pos}\nendobj\n").as_bytes());
1841        let second_xref_pos = pdf.len();
1842        pdf.extend_from_slice(
1843            format!(
1844                "xref\n\
1845                 3 1\n\
1846                 {held_pos:010} 00000 n \n\
1847                 trailer\n<< /Size 4 /Root 1 0 R /Prev 3 0 R >>\n\
1848                 startxref\n{second_xref_pos}\n%%EOF"
1849            )
1850            .as_bytes(),
1851        );
1852
1853        let mut xref_map = FxHashMap::default();
1854        let xref_pos = find_last_xref_pos(pdf.as_ref()).unwrap();
1855        assert_eq!(xref_pos, second_xref_pos);
1856        populate_xref_impl(pdf.as_ref(), xref_pos, &mut xref_map).unwrap();
1857        assert!(xref_map.contains_key(&ObjectIdentifier::new(1, 0)));
1858        assert!(xref_map.contains_key(&ObjectIdentifier::new(3, 0)));
1859    }
